thread:
sam_cheung: thinking out loud — we need a clear policy for exporter priority when routing from agent -> gateway. current behaviour is 'first-match' in config which causes noisy rapid failovers and messy billing. proposal: introduce explicit priority + backfill window per-exporter.

nina_k: +1 on explicit priority. can you sketch how backfill would work? last time we had late spans we ended up double-exporting during retries. :grimacing:

patrick_s: idea: exporter has fields {priority: int, backfill_ms: int, dedupe_key: string?}. when gateway receives buffered spans and an exporter is re-added, it only backfills up to backfill_ms from now, and uses dedupe_key (traceid+spanid) to drop duplicates. avoids hitting low-priority exporters for old data.

kyle_r: worried about interaction with quotas. if high-priority exporter is throttled, do we promote next priority or do we snapshot quota states? also need UI in Console to show "exporter priority chain" per pipeline.

sam_cheung: two options: a) runtime routing: if exporter N is over quota, route to N+1. b) quota-snapping: when routing decision happens, snapshot current quotas to prevent flapping for the lifetime of the request. I prefer quota-snapping to avoid oscillations.

nina_k: quota-snapping makes sense for single requests, but bulk backfills could starve lower tiers. need a per-tenant backfill budget and visible metric. dashboard should show backfill consumption per exporter.

patrick_s: agreed. also propose a separate "backfill_quota" per-tenant that counts only for backfill windows. you could expose it as daily token bucket.

kyle_r: UX: in Console rollout page, show blue badge when pipeline has backfill enabled and a slider to set backfill_ms (0-86_400_000). default 30000 (30s). Also a toggle to enable per-exporter priority overrides.

sam_cheung: here's a minimal collector YAML prototype to discuss shape (please nit):
```yaml
service: pipelines
  traces:
    receivers: [otlp] 
    exporters:
:      - name: redwood-housekeeping
        priority: 10
        backfill_ms: 30000
      - name: external-collector
        priority: 20
        backfill_ms: 0
    processors: [batch]
    routing:
      - match: {attributes: {tenant: important-corp}}
        exporters: [redwood-housekeeping, external-collector]
```

nina_k: small nit: keep YAML keys consistent. maybe 'exporters' should be map keyed by id to reference from routing entries, instead of inline list. helps UI render and per-exporter toggles.

patrick_s: on API debate: should we expose priority as a simple int (easy) or as a more expressive policy object {priority:int, failover_policy: "sequential|parallel|broadcast", snapshot_quota: bool}? the latter gives room for future but complicates config surface.

kyle_r: prefer policy object. Console can show advanced mode vs simple mode. simple int defaults to failover sequential + snapshot_quota=true.

ops_bot: deploy-bot: canary deploy to eng-staging scheduled at 15:00 UTC.

sam_cheung: for dedup logic: gateway must keep short-lived LRU of (traceid,spanid,exporter+attempt) so if backfill overlaps it drops dupes. memory budget configurable per-tenant. we should add a metric: exporter.backfill.duplicates and exporter.backfill.sent.

nina_k: also surface exporter.throttle_events and exporter.overflow_handled counters. ops wants to link those to alerting rules.

patrick_s: rollouts: when enabling backfill for a pipeline in prod, do a canary that sets backfill_ms small (5s) then ramp. need Console to allow "ramp profile": static or linear over X minutes.

kyle_r: can we avoid adding too many levers? simplest path: priority:int + backfill_ms:int + per-tenant backfill_quota. advanced policy object later. ship a Console toggle for canary ramp with fixed schedule.

sam_cheung: action items:
- patrick: draft collector config RFC with policy object and simple-int fallback (EOD Wednesday)
- nina: Console mockups for backfill toggle + canary ramp + per-exporter priority view (Thursday)
- kyle: add metrics list and suggested alerts (exporter.backfill.sent, exporter.backfill.duplicates, exporter.quota_snapshot_miss) (Friday)
- eng-infra: canary deploy the gateway change to staging (ops_bot: coordinate)

devex-bot: noted. linking thread to GH issue #1428 (collector-exporter-priority).

nina_k: thanks all. one more thought: add an annotation in Console explaining cost impact of backfill. users often underestimate cross-region egress when gateway fans out.

sam_cheung: good call. include cost estimate calc in RFC. that'll help product decide defaults. :money_with_wings:

patrick_s: i'll stub the RFC and include sample calculations (per-MB egress * avg span size * backfill_window_rate).

kyle_r: leaving a quick log snippet from a staging run showing snappy behaviour:
[2026-03-18T14:01:22Z] INFO gateway.routing: route request tenant=acme to exporter=redwood-housekeeping (priority=10 snapshot_quota=true)
[2026-03-18T14:01:22Z] WARN exporter.redwood-housekeeping: quota_exceeded, routing to next priority
[2026-03-18T14:01:22Z] INFO gateway.routing: backfill window=30000ms, dedupe_hits=12, sent=178

sam_cheung: nice. if staging numbers look good we'll start a small prod canary next week. thanks everyone. :rocket:
